580. Maildir rerun can recreate a message after ordinary flag changes
Batch: 9186 | Execution: 2026-10-06__23-01-03 | Type: migration-rerun-identity
Task: imap-maildir-cutover-ansible-rhel10-9186
Affected command/source nodes: node3
Contract: Move the staged archive mailbox into a working IMAP service on node1 for the
archive account. Node2 should be able to authenticate and retrieve both messages,
preserving their Message-ID values, bodies, and the read/unread state described
in mailbox.tsv. The supplied mailbox under /srv/legacy2/imap-maildir-cutover is
the only copy and must remain intact. Use a dedicated demonstration password.

Use Dovecot with encrypted IMAP access from node2 only. Node2 must validate the server certificate; a dedicated local demonstration CA is acceptable. Provision the archive account with a separate demonstration password. Preserve the staged mailbox as the recovery source; the original messages must remain byte-for-byte intact after retrieval.

If Dovecot is not installed, install the compatible packaged software from the configured, signed repositories. If it is unavailable or cannot be installed without changing platform or trust policy, stop and report the blocker rather than substitute another implementation.

Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel; use software compatible with this platform.

Implement using Ansible.
Properties: 11 Storage and data integrity, 14 Reproducibility and input closure, 15 Rerun and automation safety
Origin/transition/final context: Supplied immutable staged mailbox copied by agent-authored Ansible into mutable Dovecot Maildir names; initial expected filename is reused as the rerun identity.
Problem: The execution-level prompt at jobs/9186/2026-10-06__23-01-03/prompt explicitly requires repeated application to preserve data and avoid unnecessary changes. The playbook copies the original read message to cur/one.eml:2,S and unread message to cur/two.eml:2, with force:false. Its existence guard is the exact filename containing the initial flag suffix, not a stable message identity or completed-migration marker. Ordinary read/unread changes rename a Maildir file to another :2, flag suffix, making the original destination name absent on a later playbook run.
Observed impact: The recorded initial migration and retrieval preserve the required two source messages and flags. No recorded test changes those flags and reruns the playbook. The concern is derived from the delivered copy rules, not a measured duplicate.
Production implication: Reapplying automation after mailbox use can create another copy of an already migrated message and restore its original flag state. Automation that passes its first migration test can therefore duplicate mailbox content on a routine rerun.
Confidence: High for the recorded behavior; production consequence conditional
Limits: Conditional source-supported rerun weakness. The task deliberately specifies only two supplied messages, so hardcoding those inputs is not itself an unsupported bulk migration. Dovecot is native packaged software and initial source preservation succeeded.
